title: Screen Time and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder Among Children 9-10 Years Old: A Prospective Cohort Study
authors: Nagata JM, Chu J, Zamora G, Ganson KT, Testa A, Jackson DB, Costello CR, Murray SB, Baker FC

primary_models.name: Propensity-weighted logistic regression of new-onset OCD at 2-year follow-up on baseline phone/SM hours per day, adjusted for sociodemographics, site, baseline MDD and family psychopathology, excluding baseline OCD
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 3, Model 3 (p. 394); reported in Results p. 392 and Abstract; interpreted in Discussion pp. 392-394 (texting, video chat and social media discussed as nonsignificant on p. 394).
primary_models.design: Prospective longitudinal cohort. Screen time (IV) measured at ABCD baseline (2016-2018, ages 9-10); OCD diagnosis (DV) measured at the 2-year follow-up (2018-2020, ages 11-12). Single binary outcome at one follow-up wave, one observation per child, no repeated measures and no time x IV interaction. Because participants with OCD at baseline are excluded, the outcome is effectively new-onset OCD by year 2. Each screen modality is entered in a separate model (one IV per model).
primary_models.sample: ABCD Release 4.0, 21 U.S. sites. Of 11,875 enrolled, 2,667 were excluded for missing screen time, OCD or confounder data, leaving 9,208; Model 3 further excludes the 666 participants with OCD at baseline, giving analytic N = 8,542. Table 1 (No OCD baseline column, n = 8,542): age mean 9.93 (SD 0.63); 49.7% female, 50.3% male; White 56.9%, Latino/Hispanic 18.5%, Black 14.9%, Asian 5.3%, Native American 3.0%, Other 1.4%; parent with college education or more 84.4%; baseline major depressive disorder 0.2%; family history of psychopathology 58.9%. Full 9,208 sample: 48.9% female, White 56.5% (Abstract says 43.5% non-White; Results text says 47.8% non-White). Table 1 percentages are propensity weighted.
primary_models.iv: Baseline self-reported hours per day of each screen modality from the ABCD Youth Screen Time Survey (typical hours per day on weekdays and weekends). Weighted daily average = (weekday x 5 + weekend x 2) / 7, entered as a continuous variable in hours/day. Qualifying modalities: texting; video chatting (e.g., Skype, FaceTime); social media/social networking (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, Twitter). Baseline means (SD) in the Model 3 sample (Table 1, No OCD baseline column, n = 8,542): texting 0.21 (0.43); video chat 0.19 (0.48); social networking 0.11 (0.40) hours/day. Each modality is a separate IV; the OR is per additional hour per day.
primary_models.dv: Binary OCD diagnosis at the 2-year follow-up from the caregiver-completed computerized KSADS-5, scored to DSM-5 criteria: presence of obsessions or compulsions plus at least one of time-consuming obsessions, time-consuming compulsions, impairment, or distress. With baseline OCD cases excluded, a positive outcome is new-onset OCD. Results text: 6.1% of the sample met OCD criteria at year 2 and 4.4% developed new-onset OCD from baseline to year 2 (denominator not stated; appears to be the 9,208 sample).

primary_models.equation: logit(P(OCD_Y2[i] = 1)) = b0 + b1*phoneSM_hours[i] + b2..b6*race_ethnicity + b7*sex + b8..b12*income + b13*parent_ed + b14..b33*site + b34*baseline_MDD + b35*family_history_psychopathology (+ b36*age, per Statistical analysis text), estimated among participants without OCD at baseline, with ACS propensity weights. OR = exp(b1) per additional hour/day; phoneSM_hours is texting, video chat, or social networking in separate models.
primary_models.estimation: Multiple logistic regression in Stata 15.1. Propensity weights applied to yield estimates representative of the American Community Survey. Site entered as a covariate; no clustering or random effects for site or family described. Significance at p < .05 (bold in Table 3). No multiple-comparison correction reported across the 7 screen modalities. No interaction or stratified analyses reported. Model 1 (unadjusted, n = 9,208) and Model 2 (adjusted plus baseline OCD as covariate, n = 9,208) reported alongside in Table 3; the Abstract and Results anchor the reported aORs to Model 3, stating findings were mostly similar to Model 2.

d_transformation.conversion_formula: d = ln(OR) * sqrt(3) / pi (Chinn 2000); CI endpoints converted the same way.
d_transformation.contrast_type: per 1 additional hour/day of the baseline phone/SM modality (weighted weekday/weekend average)
d_transformation.notes: OR converts to d directly via Chinn without p0 or SDs. SD_IV for the Model 3 analytic sample comes from Table 1 (p. 393), No OCD (baseline) column, n = 8,542: texting 0.43, video chat 0.48, social networking 0.40 hours/day; these are recorded in case a per-SD rescaling (ln(OR) * SD_IV) is wanted, since 1 hour/day is more than 2 SD for every phone/SM modality here. p0 = 0.044 is the Results-text rate of new-onset OCD from baseline to year 2 (p. 392); the denominator is not stated and may be the 9,208 sample rather than the 8,542 Model 3 sample. SD_DV not applicable (binary DV). Completion pass: all Model 3 OR/CI/exact p verified against Table 3; no SE or z printed in the PDF; CI available so no CI-input needed.

extraction_flags: 1) Which model to use: I extracted Table 3 Model 3 (n=8,542, baseline OCD cases excluded, so the outcome is new-onset OCD), because the Abstract and Results report Model 3's aORs. Model 2 (n=9,208, baseline OCD entered as a covariate) is also adjusted. I put it in excluded_models with its values in case coders prefer it. 2) Age is listed as a covariate in the Statistical analysis text, but it is missing from the Table 3 footnote and from the Abstract. Check whether it was actually in the model. 3) Videos (YouTube) and video games are excluded as non-phone/non-SM, following the paper 156 reference. However, the stage2_reason cites them, and FT-IC2 names YouTube as a platform. Coders should confirm that "Videos (YouTube)" (watching videos, e.g., YouTube, on any device) does not qualify. Its Model 3 aOR is 1.11 (1.01-1.23), p=.038. 4) None of the three phone/SM estimates is significant. Texting comes closest: aOR 1.20 (1.00-1.44), p=.056. 5) p0=0.044 is from the Results text and its denominator is unclear (probably the 9,208 sample). It is not needed for the Chinn OR-to-d conversion. 6) The SD_IV values come from the Table 1 No-OCD-baseline column (n=8,542), which is the Model 3 sample. Because the contrast is per 1 hour/day and that is more than 2 SD for every modality, the derived d per hour is large relative to the typical exposure. 7) The paper is inconsistent on percent non-White: the Abstract says 43.5% (matches Table 1) and the Results text says 47.8%. 8) No multiple-comparison correction across the 7 modalities. Site was entered as a covariate, not as a random effect.
